newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of East Asia seen in HK$2 bln FRCD.
newsitem.headline: Bank of East Asia seen in HK$2 bln FRCD.

text.p: Bank of East Asia Ltd is planning to raise funds with a floating rate certificate of deposit issue, sources close to the transaction said on Tuesday.
They said the issue size is expected to be at least HK$2 billion, with an effective tenor of three years.
The borrower is expected to apply to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the issue as eligible for the HKMA's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the HKMA, increasing liquidity.
Bank of East Asia is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service.
Sources said the issue is expected to be launched into the market in the first half of this year.
Schroders Asia recently privately placed a non-LAF floating rate certificate of deposit issue for Bank of East Asia.
